name: Constancy in knowledge of what pertains to the self (BhG 13.12)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Listed among the twenty dispositions called 'knowledge': constancy in knowledge of what pertains to the self (adhyātma-jñāna-nityatva), together with keeping in view the aim of the knowledge of reality (13.12). 15.5 counts those 'constantly intent on what pertains to the self' (adhyātmanitya) among those who reach the imperishable place. The text gives no further method.

name: Cutting the aśvattha with the weapon of non-attachment (BhG 15.3–5)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The text gives the method as an image: the firmly rooted aśvattha (roots above, branches below, swollen by the guṇas, sense-objects its shoots, its roots below bound up with action) is to be cut with the strong weapon of non-attachment (asaṅga-śastra); then the place from which there is no return is to be sought, in the words 'I take refuge in that very primal person from whom the ancient activity flowed forth'. No further technique is given.

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch13-15): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

signs_of_progress: Free from pride and delusion, the fault of attachment conquered, constantly intent on what pertains to the self, desires turned away, released from the pairs of pleasure and pain — such undeluded ones go to the imperishable place (15.5).

name: Discerning the field and its knower (kṣetra-kṣetrajña)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Knowing the field (the body and its constituents, 13.2, 13.6-13.7) and its knower is called knowledge (13.3). Whoever knows puruṣa and prakṛti with the guṇas thus is not born again (13.24). The one who truly sees sees the supreme lord abiding equally in all beings (13.28), actions as done by prakṛti alone and oneself as not the doer (13.30), and the separate existence of beings as resting in the one (13.31). Those who know the difference between field and knower with the eye of knowledge go to the highest (13.35).
signs_of_progress: Not born again (13.24); reaching brahman (13.31); going to the highest (13.35).

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch13-15): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

equivalents.note: The Mokṣadharma's practice of enumerating the twenty-four principles and knowing the twenty-fifth as other than them corresponds to knowing the difference between the field (13.6–7, whose items can be counted as twenty-four) and its knower (13.35); the Gītā gives no number and speaks of field and knower, not of principles.

notes: New practice (extractor B) in the Gītā's own terms.

name: Seeing that the guṇas act: non-doership
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Whoever sees actions done by prakṛti alone and oneself as not the doer sees truly (13.30); the seer who sees no doer other than the guṇas and knows what is beyond them attains the Lord's state (14.19); the one beyond the guṇas sits as one indifferent, unshaken, knowing only that 'the guṇas are operating' (14.23).
